## 4. Time Series
```{python}
#| label: timeseries-gpp-ndvi-evi

# data

print("project_dir:", project_dir)
print("current_dir:", Path.cwd())

print(
    "File exists:",
    (project_dir / "data" / "processed" / "site_daily.csv").exists()
)


site_daily = pd.read_csv(
    project_dir / "data" / "processed" / "site_daily.csv", parse_dates=["date"]
)

# MODIS available period for each site

ch_fru = site_daily[
    (site_daily["site_id"] == "CH-Fru") &
    (site_daily["date"] >= "2022-01-01") &
    (site_daily["date"] <= "2024-12-31")
].copy()

il_yat = site_daily[
    (site_daily["site_id"] == "IL-Yat") &
    (site_daily["date"] >= "2022-01-01") &
    (site_daily["date"] <= "2024-12-31")
].copy()

it_bci = site_daily[
    (site_daily["site_id"] == "IT-BCi") &
    (site_daily["date"] >= "2024-01-01") &
    (site_daily["date"] <= "2026-11-01")
].copy()

jp_smf = site_daily[
    (site_daily["site_id"] == "JP-SMF") &
    (site_daily["date"] >= "2012-01-01") &
    (site_daily["date"] <= "2014-12-31")
].copy()

us_moz = site_daily[
    (site_daily["site_id"] == "US-MOz") &
    (site_daily["date"] >= "2019-01-01") &
    (site_daily["date"] <= "2021-12-31")
].copy()



# plot

fig, axes = plt.subplots(
    5, 1,
    figsize=(12, 15)
)

dfs = [
    ("CH-Fru", ch_fru),
    ("IL-Yat", il_yat),
    ("IT-BCi", it_bci),
    ("JP-SMF", jp_smf),
    ("US-MOz", us_moz)
]

for ax, (site, df) in zip(axes, dfs):

    ax.plot(
        df["date"],
        df["GPP_NT_VUT_REF"],
        color="forestgreen",
        label="GPP"
    )

    ax.set_title(site)

    ax_r = ax.twinx()

    ax_r.plot(
        df["date"],
        df["ndvi"],
        color="orange",
        label="NDVI"
    )

    ax_r.plot(
        df["date"],
        df["evi"],
        color="royalblue",
        label="EVI"
    )

    ax_r.set_ylim(0, 1)

    ax.set_ylabel("GPP (g C m$^{-2}$ d$^{-1}$)")

    ax_r.set_ylabel("NDVI / EVI", color="black")


fig.suptitle(
    "Relationship between GPP and MODIS Vegetation Indices",
    fontsize=16,
    fontweight="bold"
)   

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

```

### Interpretation of graph

* CH-Fru, JP-SMF, and US-MOz showed a strong seasonal correspondence between GPP and the vegetation indices (NDVI and EVI). In these sites, both indices generally followed the seasonal dynamics of GPP, with higher values during the growing season and lower values during winter.
* In contrast, IL-Yat and IT-BCi exhibited a weaker relationship between vegetation indices and GPP. NDVI and EVI describe canopy greenness, whereas GPP measures carbon uptake through photosynthesis. Therefore, periods of high canopy greenness did not always coincide with maximum photosynthetic activity, indicating a partial decoupling between vegetation structure and ecosystem productivity.


## 5. One Question : Extreme events
```{python}
#| label: read-data-dheed-extreme-events
#| fig-cap: "Daily NEE, GPP and RECO (g C m⁻² d⁻¹) for the site"

moz = site_daily[
    site_daily["site_id"] == "US-MOz"
].copy()


event = moz[
    moz["dheed_event"] == True
]

event_start = event["date"].min()
event_end   = event["date"].max()

print("event start day :", event_start)
print("event end day :", event_end)

moz_event = moz[
    moz["date"].dt.year.isin([2011, 2012, 2013])
].copy()




window = (
    (moz_event["date"].dt.month == 7) &
    (moz_event["date"].dt.day >= 17)
) | (
    (moz_event["date"].dt.month == 8) &
    (moz_event["date"].dt.day <= 2)
)


box = moz_event[window].copy()

box["year"] = box["date"].dt.year
box["period"] = box["year"].astype(str)

box.loc[
    box["year"] == 2012,
    "period"
] = "2012 DHEED"

#plotting
fig,(ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(6, 5))

sns.boxplot(
    data=box,
    x="period",
    y="GPP_NT_VUT_REF",ax=ax1
)

sns.boxplot(
    data=box,
    x="period",
    y="NEE_VUT_REF",ax=ax2
)

ax1.set_title("GPP")
ax2.set_title("NEE")

ax1.set_ylabel("GPP (g C m$^{-2}$ d$^{-1}$)")
ax2.set_ylabel("NEE (g C m$^{-2}$ d$^{-1}$)")

ax1.set_xlabel("Year")
ax2.set_xlabel("Year")

fig.suptitle(
    "Fluxes during Jul 17–Aug 02\n(US-MOz DHEED comparison)",
    fontsize=14
)
plt.show()




```



### Results

**1. Target Site and Analysis Background**

US-MOz is a flux tower located in Missouri, USA, within a deciduous broadleaf forest ecosystem characterized by hot, humid summers and relatively cold winters. During the observation period (2004–2021), only one extreme event meeting the DHEED criteria was identified. This event occurred from 17 July to 2 August 2012. To assess its ecological impacts, ecosystem responses during the event period were compared with those observed during the same calendar period in the years before and after the event.

**2. Results comparison 2012(DHeed period) vs  2011, 1013**
The 2012 DHEED period showed lower GPP, less negative NEE, higher VPD, and higher air temperature than the same calendar periods in 2011 and 2013.

**3. limitation of results**

1. No clear evidence of a drought legacy effect was observed in 2013 at US-MOz. However, legacy effects were evaluated only using one post-event year (2013), making it difficult to determine whether longer-term impacts occurred.

2. Problem of different spatial resolution (Detailed in the following section 6)  


## 6. Scale of Dataset

| Dataset | Spatial Resolution |
|----------|----------|
| ERA5-Land | 0.1° (~9 km) |
| WorldClim 2.1 | 5′ (~9 km) |
| DHEED | 0.25° (~28 km) |
| SoilGrids 2.0 | 250 m |
| PlantTraits | 1 km |
| iNaturalist | Point observations (variable location) |
| MODIS MOD13Q1 | 250 m (native resolution); 9 × 9 pixel window (~2.25 × 2.25 km) used in this study |

** what does it mean to my question? **

DHEED events were identified using ERA5 grid cells (0.25° ≈ 25 km × 25 km), whereas flux measurements represent local ecosystem conditions within a footprint of only a few hundred metres. Consequently, a DHEED event detected for the grid cell may not necessarily indicate that the tower footprint experienced the same intensity of stress. Conversely, local ecosystem stress observed at the tower may not always be captured by the coarser DHEED grid. Therefore, scale mismatches introduce uncertainty when linking DHEED events to observed ecosystem responses.
